references.text: Isaiah 53:11 describes how the servant's suffering will lead him to see the light and be satisfied, paralleling the idea of losing one's life to find it in Christ.
Matthew 16:25 repeats the same principle as in Matthew 10:39, that losing one's life for Jesus' sake will lead to finding it.
Luke 9:24 reinforces the message of Matthew 10:39 by saying that whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for Jesus' sake will save it.
John 12:25 highlights the contrast between loving one's life to death and hating one's life in this world to keep it for eternal life, paralleling losing and finding life in Matthew 10:39.
Galatians 2:19-20 speaks of being crucified with Christ and no longer living oneself, but Christ living in the believer, resonating with giving up one's own life to find true life in Christ.
